summary.text: Kepler's laws are the laws of planetary orbits that Johannes Kepler developed from physical principles and Tycho Brahe's observations of the planets.
His elliptical model of planetary motion greatly improved the accuracy of predictions, years before Newton developed his law of gravitation in 1686.
Newton later confirmed the laws for elliptical orbits by deriving them from the gravitational two-body problem in his Principia of 1687.

facts.label: Developed by
facts.value: Johannes Kepler, using Tycho Brahe's planetary observations

facts.label: Kepler's model
facts.value: Planetary motion described with an elliptical model

items.prompt: Before Kepler, careful predictions of planet positions had little link to arguments about what physically moves them. How did Kepler change that?

options.label: He dropped prediction and argued only about causes
He replaced geometry with arithmetic tables
He joined predictive geometrical astronomy with physical concepts
He proved that gravity pulls apples and planets alike

items.explain: Kepler was the first to closely integrate predictive geometrical astronomy with physical concepts, in his 1609 New Astronomy.

items.prompt: Kepler needed measurements of where planets really were to build his laws. Whose observations did he rely on?

options.label: Ptolemy
Copernicus
Tycho Brahe
Isaac Newton

items.explain: Kepler developed the laws using his physical principles and the planetary observations made by Tycho Brahe.

items.prompt: A student says Kepler's predictions only became reliable once Newton's gravity explained them. What is wrong with that claim?

options.label: Newton published his gravity law decades before Kepler's laws
Kepler's model never improved predictions, even afterwards
Newton only repeated Kepler's observations without deriving anything
The elliptical model had already improved predictions years before Newton's law of gravitation

items.explain: Kepler's elliptical model greatly improved predictions years before Newton developed his law of gravitation.

items.prompt: How did Newton show that Kepler's laws for elliptical orbits were right?

options.label: By repeating Brahe's observations with a better instrument
By deriving them from his law of gravity applied to two bodies
By showing that orbits are circles after all
By adding a third body and solving the motion exactly

items.explain: Using his law of gravity, Newton derived the laws from the gravitational two-body problem in the Principia.

items.prompt: A comet follows a parabolic path instead of a closed loop. How does this path relate to the orbits Kepler described?

options.label: It is a conic-section extension of his ellipses
It breaks his laws entirely, so none of them applies
It is a circle seen from an angle
It is the same ellipse traced faster

items.explain: Parabolic and hyperbolic orbits are conic section extensions of Kepler's elliptical orbits.

items.prompt: Astronomers use Newtonian mechanics to compute the future positions of two bodies pulling on each other. What does this method show about Kepler's laws?

options.label: That they fail once gravity is properly included
That they only work for planets moving in circles
That relativity is needed for them to hold
That the laws are correct

items.explain: This method demonstrates the correctness of Kepler's laws of planetary motion.
